A nice bass I pulled out last month. Shame I didn't realize my hand obscured his tail.
First time fishing this year and I snagged this guy on a rubber worm deep in the Lilly pads. After about 10 minutes we finally up anchored and dug him out of the tangled vines.

Those rubber worms are seemingly irresistible to bass. Not that bass won't hit just about anything, but I've had some ridiculously good luck with rubber worms. Also, some of the lakes I've been fishing are so shallow and weedy, you basically can't use a lure.

Is that a smallmouth you caught in this picture? It's coloring is much darker than I'm used to seeing. Bass are always fun to reel in.

I've been really hit and miss with soft baits. They seem to be a lot more effective than the fancy spinner and buzz baits.

But I sometimes have trouble fine tuneing the technique of slowly inching forward. That being said, they've produced the best bass I've ever reeled in.

Yeah weeds and brush can be a nightmare. And a Texas rigged worm is sometimes the only option in that situation. But it allows you to breach basically safe haven for bass.

You know I always thought it was a large mouth, but that I look at it again the mouth doesn't extend that far. So I would agree It's a smallmouth.

I'd never heard it called "Texas Rigged" before, but when I looked it up, that is exactly the way I always set up the worm.

What I normally do is just cast right into the weeds, maybe 4 to 6 feet of water, and let it sink to the bottom. If you haven't caught a bass yet, reel in and cast again. They either hit it immediately, or not at all. Everyone has their color they swear by, and I'm no different. The green/yellow ones are the best.

I found this picture that shows the different soft-bait methods. Sinker, with a covered/weedless hook is Texas all right.

However a certain bass hole I know of does produce most strikes while the lure is falling.

But if it's a nice clear lake you really gotta use more natural colors.
